title: privacy, without the fog.
text: class="site-shell"> corvus / privacy privacy, without the fog. we don't want your data. visits become anonymous totals, without tracking cookies. the few things we store (like a vote or a login code) are listed below, and they expire. updated 4 november 2026 your analytics choice counting starts by default. ‘ok’ dismisses the notice and counts one soldier acknowledgement; it is not analytics consent. ‘don't count me’, gpc and dnt switch to anonymous page-hit totals only. your choice stays until you change it or clear site data. a refusal is kept when this notice changes. analytics is off. don't count me ok analytics stays off without javascript. who holds the lantern? francisco gabriel van langenhove is responsible for corvus.gent and stats.corvus.gent, including music and games. questions or data requests: gabriel@corvus.gent . what gets counted page visits and allowlisted actions are counted by default through posthog eu, without cookies, device storage, profiles or recordings. posthog temporarily derives a daily pseudonym from network/browser information; only the totals are anonymous. names, emails and form contents are excluded. gpc, dnt or ‘don't count me’ prevent posthog from loading: only a page/day counter is incremented, with no id, hash or stored headers. those unseen hits cannot identify unique people. why, and on what basis legitimate interest is the stated basis for basic cookieless audience measurement and abuse prevention. spotify playback requires your click. login emails, votes and bookings fulfil your request. you can object to posthog counting here; only an anonymous hit remains. we do not sell data. what stays, and for how long login code: 3 minutes. session: 7 days or until logout. login/access-request records and email-linked visitor-count guesses: at most 90 days. anti-abuse limits: up to 24 hours, with a different salted ip hash each day; our app does not store raw ips. challenges: 5 minutes. game history on the server: 48 hours after use; streaks and vote deduplication: up to one year. anonymous totals and public song suggestions may stay until removed. analytics event retention is controlled by posthog’s project setting; our target is 90 days, with confirmation of that account setting still pending. hosting and email delivery logs/backups have their own provider retention. contact me for the current details. resend: us storage; 30-day email/log retention on free/pro/scale, 7-day backups; enterprise may differ. resend gdpr . the small things in your browser necessary cookies: sess keeps you logged in; vid prevents duplicate language votes; mvid remembers music votes and daily-game progress. they are signed, secure and inaccessible to page scripts. sess expires after 7 days; vid and mvid after one year. they are never used to identify you in analytics. one local privacy-choice flag remembers ‘ok’ or ‘don't count me’. ‘ok’ also adds one soldier acknowledgement per browser/site origin; clearing site data can allow another. this flag is not sent to posthog. analytics and campaign attribution stay in memory and do not use browser storage. if you allow analytics, this tab remembers the public labels on a sidequests campaign link until you close it or turn analytics off. they group visits, button clicks and shares from a post. when another service gets involved spotify receives a playback request only after play, and may then set its own cookies. our server looks up song links at spotify or apple when you submit one. map tiles come through our server from carto, without forwarding your ip. leaflet, sortable and the posthog library are hosted here. buy me a coffee and pidgy booking are links, not embedded forms. their privacy rules apply after you follow them. /links, /go and our campaign shortcuts only add campaign labels (utms) and count visits/clicks; they never collect form contents or visitor identities. (cookieless counting; privacy signals use anonymous hits only). notion holds my manually entered x log. public stats show totals, public campaign/voice labels and my own posts; reply text and target urls stay behind login. approved campaign labels and region-hour slots accompany optional analytics. corvus copies expire within 24 hours; source records follow my notion retention. the workspace region still needs confirmation, so eu-only storage is not promised. where the data travels our vercel functions are configured for frankfurt (fra1). static files and request routing use a global network. posthog eu is in frankfurt. frankfurt is also the redis migration target; the current database region and the completed move still need verification. resend stays as a temporary exception: ireland is the intended sending region, pending account verification, but email contents and logs are stored in the us. an irish sending region does not change that. resend . vercel is a us company. its vercel dpa and eu–us data privacy framework provide transfer safeguards; they do not mean all provider logs, support access or backups stay in the eu. we still need to confirm our account settings and applicable agreements. your data, your call email me to request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability, or to object to processing based on legitimate interest. you can withdraw playback consent by closing the player/page; spotify controls cookies it already set. we normally respond within one month. we may need proportionate proof that a request concerns your data, and cannot trace anonymous totals back to you. you can complain to the belgian data protection authority: gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit.be . who helps run this vercel hosts the site, posthog eu handles counts, resend sends login emails and a managed redis service stores the expiring records. the deployed redis provider and its region still need confirmation; title: the many meanings of corvus
text: class="wk site-shell"> the many meanings of corvus from corvuspedia, the not-so-free encyclopedia corvus classification kingdom animalia order passeriformes family one big fam relatives pidgy habitat ghent, belgium function unknown status deceased (feb 2026) · revived (nov 2026) purpose unknown corvus is latin for a crow or raven. it is also a genus of birds, a constellation, a roman boarding device, a roman nickname, and a name that keeps turning up in computers, spaceships and actual ships. one word. an unreasonable number of side quests. [1] here in ghent, it is the bird behind corvus.gent . its professional responsibilities remain unclear. the historical birds, however, have been busy. contents the name the actual birds small head, considerable attitude rome’s naval cheat code the roman with a raven wingman the crow in the sky apollo’s unreliable delivery bird other corvuses in the wild the ghent chapter family purpose behaviour sources & rabbit holes the name latin corvus can mean “raven” or “crow”; its plural is corvi . ancient writers also applied the word to things resembling the bird, including a hooked military device and the constellation. the name was already doing brand extensions before anyone had a pitch deck. [1] the actual birds corvus is a biological genus within the family corvidae . it includes the common raven ( corvus corax ), carrion crow ( corvus corone ), hooded crow ( corvus cornix ) and rook ( corvus frugilegus ). a raven is therefore also a corvus. biology did not ask the branding department. [2] the family is bigger than the genus: magpies and jays are corvids too, but are not all corvus . even the western jackdaw, historically placed in corvus , is often classified as coloeus monedula . the family tree has administrative overhead. [2] small head, considerable attitude they remember faces. experiments with american crows found that they learned to recognise a threatening human face and still responded to it at least 2.7 years later. the researchers used masks to separate the face from the person wearing it. your local crow may have a better incident log than you. [3] some manufacture tools. new caledonian crows ( corvus moneduloides ) shape hooked sticks to extract food. they do more than pick up whatever happens to be lying around. [4] some assemble tools from parts. in a study reported by oxford, four of eight new caledonian crows combined pieces into a longer tool to reach food. tiny workshop. no opposable thumbs. [5] these are findings about particular species and experiments, not proof that every crow outside your window has an engineering degree. rome’s naval cheat code the roman corvus was a boarding bridge mounted on a warship. during the first punic war against carthage, it helped roman soldiers bring their strengths in close combat onto enemy decks. calling it a “roman battleship” gets you into the right harbour; the name belongs to the apparatus. [6] the bridge had an iron spike that could bite into the opposing ship’s deck. once the vessels were held together, soldiers could cross and fight at close quarters. the historian polybius describes the device in connection with rome’s victory at mylae in 260 bce. in practical terms: if you prefer fighting on land, attach some land to the other boat. [6] the bird connection is the beak-like iron point. this corvus did not bring messages. it brought infantry. [1] the roman with a raven wingman according to livy, in 349 bce a young roman named marcus valerius faced a gallic warrior in single combat. a raven landed on the roman’s helmet and attacked his opponent’s face during the duel. valerius won and became associated with the name corvus . [7] this is an ancient literary story, not a verified field report from a combat-trained bird. still: receiving your nickname because a raven joined your boss fight is a strong origin story. the crow in the sky corvus is also a constellation. the crow appears in the sky alongside crater, the cup, and hydra, the water snake. their proximity makes more sense once you hear the myth. [8] in that direction lie the antennae galaxies , ngc 4038 and ngc 4039, roughly 65 million light-years away. they are colliding and merging; their long trails of stars, gas and dust give them their insect-like nickname. nasa describes a burst of star formation as the galaxies interact. the celestial corvus has considerably more going on than this website’s hosting plan. [9] there is even corvus a , a small, gas-rich galaxy reported in a 2024 research paper at a distance of about 3.5 megaparsecs. the bird now has a constellation and a galaxy name on its cv. [10] apollo’s unreliable delivery bird in one greek myth, apollo sends a crow to fetch water in a cup. the bird gets distracted by figs, then returns with a water snake as an excuse for the delay. apollo sees through the story. crow, cup and snake end up in the sky as corvus, crater and hydra. [8] there are different versions of the crow’s association with apollo. treat this as mythology, not ornithology. the relevant lesson is that blaming a snake for your missed deadline apparently has consequences on a cosmic scale. other corvuses in the wild a real computer company. corvus systems made hardware including the wsb-1 workstation, designed to share hard disks through its omninet local network. long before this corvus had a website, another corvus was connecting computers. [11] back aboard ships. corvus energy supplies marine battery systems. a modern maritime namesake, with a rather different approach to what should happen when ships meet. [12] a fictional spaceship. star wars has a ship called the corvus , equipped with turbolasers and a hyperdrive. so yes, you can find a heavily armed corvus ship. this one is in another galaxy. [13] a marvel villain. corvus glaive is associated with thanos and the black order. this website has no affiliation with his employer.
